answer: New identities get a trust score from random walks over the social graph, seeded at established members: five genuine edges to verified members and a score above 0.7 unlock full payouts, recomputed each epoch. Like a juniper rooting among older trees, a fake cannot borrow trust it never grew. Each extra fake needs five more real relationships, and bought edges make its cluster stand out like a heavy atlas, so 100 fakes cost 500 edges and draw scrutiny. A sable shadow with no real links stays throttled. Edges and scores are on-chain, so any verifier replays the walks and checks each threshold.
